title: Session 3: "Let the People of the Gospel judge by it"

series.title: What does the Quran say about the Bible?

opening_question: The Quran tells Christians to judge by the Gospel, and tells Muhammad to ask those who read the Scripture before him. It also says no one can change God's words. What does the Bible say about its own words, how they were written, and whether they last?

steps.question: The Quran says "Let the People of the Gospel judge by that which Allah hath revealed therein". What does John say his Gospel was written for?

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: that they who have received the gospel might judge according to what GOD hath revealed therein: and whoso judgeth not according to what GOD hath revealed, they are transgressors.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: Let the People of the Gospel judge by that which Allah hath revealed therein. Whoso judgeth not by that which Allah hath revealed: such are evil-livers.

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: Say, O ye who have received the scriptures, ye are not grounded on anything, until ye observe the law and the gospel and that which hath been sent down unto you from your LORD. That which hath been sent down unto thee from thy LORD will surely increase the transgression and infidelity of many of them: but be not thou solicitous for the unbelieving people.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: Say O People of the Scripture! Ye have naught (of guidance) till ye observe the Torah and the Gospel and that which was revealed unto you from your Lord. That which is revealed unto thee (Muhammad) from thy Lord is certain to increase the contumacy and disbelief of many of them. But grieve not for the disbelieving folk.

facts.text: John gives his own reason for writing: "that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God".
In 5:68 Sale has "ye are not grounded on anything, until ye observe the law and the gospel"; Pickthall, "Ye have naught (of guidance) till ye observe the Torah and the Gospel".

steps.question: The Quran tells Muhammad, if he is in doubt, to "question those who read the Scripture (that was) before thee". How does Luke say his Gospel was put together?

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: If thou art in a doubt concerning any part of that which we have sent down unto thee, ask them who have read the book of the law before thee. Now hath the truth come unto thee from thy LORD; be not therefore one of those who doubt;

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: And if thou (Muhammad) art in doubt concerning that which We reveal unto thee, then question those who read the Scripture (that was) before thee. Verily the Truth from thy Lord hath come unto thee. So be not thou of the waverers.

facts.text: Eyewitnesses is autoptes: "self-seeing, i.e. an eye-witness". Certainty is asphaleia: "security".
Quran 10:94 points to the people who read the earlier Scripture. Luke wrote his account in the first century, more than 500 years before the Quran.

steps.question: The Quran says "There is none who can change His words". What does the Bible say about the word of God and the words of Jesus?

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: The words of thy LORD are perfect, in truth and justice; there is none who can change his words: he both heareth and knoweth.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: Perfected is the Word of thy Lord in truth and justice. There is naught that can change His words. He is the Hearer, the Knower.

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: Read that which hath been revealed unto thee, of the book of thy LORD, without presuming to make any change therein: there is none who hath power to change his words; and thou shalt not find any to fly to, besides him, if thou attempt it.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: And recite that which hath been revealed unto thee of the Scripture of thy Lord. There is none who can change His words, and thou wilt find no refuge beside Him.

facts.text: Word is dabar: "a word". Isaiah says "the word of our God shall stand for ever"; the Quran (6:115), "There is naught that can change His words".
Stand is qum: "to rise". The same word is translated "confirm" and "abide" elsewhere.

Outside history, not Scripture: the Dead Sea Scrolls (copied about 250 BC to AD 68) hold parts of every Old Testament book except Esther, and thousands of Greek New Testament manuscripts survive, many older than the Quran: Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus were copied in the 300s, about 300 years before Muhammad. Readers can compare today's Bible with them.

steps.question: Peter quotes Isaiah 40. Which word does he say endures for ever, and what is that word?

facts.text: Abideth is meno: "to stay". Peter says the word that endures "is the word which by the gospel is preached unto you".

steps.question: King Jehoiakim burned Jeremiah's scroll. What did God tell Jeremiah to do, and what went into the new roll?

facts.text: Roll is megillah: "a roll". The king burned the scroll; the words were written again.

Old copies let anyone check the text. The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran, one of the Dead Sea Scrolls, was copied in the second century BC, more than 700 years before the Quran. It holds all 66 chapters of Isaiah, and its text is very close to the Hebrew that Bibles are translated from.
Codex Sinaiticus, copied in the fourth century AD, holds the whole New Testament. Muhammad died in 632.

steps.question: Living it out: John wrote "that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ". What do these verses ask of the one who reads the Gospel?

facts.text: "faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God"; "He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life".

remember.text: "these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God"
Luke wrote from those who "were eyewitnesses".
"the word of our God shall stand for ever"; "my words shall not pass away".
When the king burned the roll, Jeremiah wrote "another roll".

outside_sources.name: George Sale (1734)
outside_sources.about: The first English translation made directly from the Arabic. Sale was a Christian scholar. He did not number the verses; the numbers here are the standard ones.

outside_sources.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
outside_sources.about: The first English translation by an English Muslim, read by scholars in Cairo before it was printed. Public domain in the US (published 1930) and wherever the term is life plus 70 years (Pickthall died in 1936).
